title: Positive Psychology in a Pandemic, with Martin Seligman, PhD

sentences.en: Over the past 20 years, the field of positive psychology has grown from a fledgling idea to a worldwide movement.
sentences.zh: 在过去的20年里，积极心理学领域已经从一个初出茅庐的理念成长为一场全球性的运动。

sentences.en: Positive psychology is the scientific study of the strengths that enable individuals and communities to thrive.
sentences.zh: 积极心理学是对使个人和社区能够茁壮成长的优势的科学研究。

sentences.en: It is based on the idea that psychological research can help us understand the characteristics and qualities that allow people to lead more meaningful and fulfilling lives,
sentences.zh: 它基于这样一个理念：心理学研究可以帮助我们理解那些让人们过上更有意义、更充实生活的特征和品质，

sentences.en: and then design techniques to help them do that.
sentences.zh: 并据此设计出帮助人们实现这一目标的技巧。

sentences.en: After a year when many of us have had a hard time staying optimistic, most of us would welcome any tips on how to become more positive.
sentences.zh: 在过去这一年里，我们许多人都难以保持乐观，大多数人都很乐意听到关于如何变得更积极的建议。

sentences.en: What does positive psychology have to say about flourishing in tough times, such as a pandemic?
sentences.zh: 积极心理学对于在像大流行这样的艰难时期如何蓬勃发展有什么见解吗？

sentences.en: And for people who are not optimistic by nature, is there anything they can do to become more positive?
sentences.zh: 对于那些天生不乐观的人来说，他们能做些什么来变得更积极吗？

sentences.en: Does being positive offer particular benefits, such as perhaps greater resistance to viruses?
sentences.zh: 保持积极心态会带来特别的好处吗，比如对病毒有更强的抵抗力？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Martin Seligman, professor of psychology at the University of Pennsylvania and director of the Penn Positive Psychology Center.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是宾夕法尼亚大学心理学教授、宾大积极心理学中心主任马丁·塞利格曼博士。

sentences.en: He's been called the founder of positive psychology and has published more than 350 scholarly publications and 30 books,
sentences.zh: 他被称为积极心理学之父，发表了350多篇学术论文，出版了30多本书，

sentences.en: including his latest and autobiography called The Hope Circuit, which you can find on Amazon.
sentences.zh: 包括他最新的自传《希望回路》，你可以在亚马逊上找到。

sentences.en: He was also president of the American Psychological Association in 1998,
sentences.zh: 他还在1998年担任过美国心理学会主席，

sentences.en: during which one of his presidential initiatives was the promotion of positive psychology as a field of scientific study.
sentences.zh: 任期内他的总统倡议之一就是推动积极心理学作为一门科学研究领域的发展。

sentences.en: He is also a leading authority in the fields of resilience, learned helplessness, depression, optimism, and pessimism.
sentences.zh: 他也是韧性、习得性无助、抑郁、乐观和悲观领域的权威专家。

sentences.en: And he is a recognized authority on interventions that prevent depression and build strengths and well-being.
sentences.zh: 同时，他也是预防抑郁、建立优势和幸福感的干预措施方面的公认权威。

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, Dr. Seligman.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到《心理学谈话》，塞利格曼博士。

sentences.en: Oh, thank you, Kim.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢你，金。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: Let's start with one of the questions I posed in the introduction.
sentences.zh: 让我们从我在介绍中提出的一个问题开始。

sentences.en: It's been more than a year since the SARS-CoV-2 virus was identified, and while vaccines are providing a good deal of hope, there's still a long winter ahead of us.
sentences.zh: 距离SARS-CoV-2病毒被发现已经过去一年多了，虽然疫苗带来了很大的希望，但我们前方依然有一个漫长的冬天。

sentences.en: What lessons can people take from positive psychology that they can use to get through the next few months?
sentences.zh: 人们可以从积极心理学中汲取哪些经验来度过接下来的几个月？

sentences.en: Well, positive psychology has a lot to say about COVID and what we should be doing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，积极心理学对于新冠疫情以及我们应该做什么有很多见解。

sentences.en: And I should say, Kim, that I'm personally, this is quite a tale for me.
sentences.zh: 我得说，金，对我个人而言，这真是一个曲折的故事。

sentences.en: We made the mistake of having Thanksgiving with all of our five kids.
sentences.zh: 我们犯了个错误，和五个孩子一起过了感恩节。

sentences.en: Good thing to do.
sentences.zh: 本以为是件好事。

sentences.en: We all got tested before my son came in from Chicago.
sentences.zh: 我儿子从芝加哥回来之前，我们都做了检测。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, he had it.
sentences.zh: 结果他突然就感染了。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.en: And all five of my kids and my wife came down with COVID, whereupon they kicked me out of the house,
sentences.zh: 我的五个孩子和我妻子都感染了新冠，于是他们把我赶出了家门，

sentences.en: and I evacuated to a hotel for 17 days until they were past the period of recovery.
sentences.zh: 我撤离到一家酒店住了17天，直到他们过了恢复期。

sentences.en: And I just returned about a week ago.
sentences.zh: 我大约一周前才回来。

sentences.en: And I've been in quarantine since March 1St.
sentences.zh: 从3月1日起我就一直在隔离。

sentences.en: And so COVID has been quite an experience for this family, and I expect it to be going on through about the spring.
sentences.zh: 所以新冠对我们家来说是一次相当深刻的经历，我预计这种情况会持续到春天。

sentences.en: So my task is to hold out until I can get the jab.
sentences.zh: 所以我的任务就是坚持到能打上疫苗为止。

sentences.en: I hope that'll be in March, and then we can resume life.
sentences.zh: 我希望那会在三月，然后我们就能恢复正常生活了。

sentences.en: But let me say what positive psychology has told us, and I think the science tells people about COVID.
sentences.zh: 但让我说说积极心理学告诉了我们什么，我认为科学告诉了人们关于新冠的什么。

sentences.en: First, I think when one talks about positive psychology, it's important to make nuanced distinctions about different kinds of well-being.
sentences.zh: 首先，我认为当谈论积极心理学时，对不同类型的幸福感进行细致的区分是很重要的。

sentences.en: And the one I'm about to make is the difference between smiley, merry, cheerful, being happy, called positive, affective, and optimistic, forward-looking, which is not a feeling.
sentences.zh: 我即将做出的区分是：微笑、快乐、愉悦、幸福感（称为积极情感），与乐观、展望未来（这并非一种感觉）。

sentences.en: It's a cognition about the future.
sentences.zh: 这是一种关于未来的认知。

sentences.en: It's about hope.
sentences.zh: 这是关于希望。

sentences.en: Now, those are both positive, but they have different effects, particularly with respect to different illnesses.
sentences.zh: 这两者都是积极的，但它们有不同的影响，特别是在针对不同疾病方面。

sentences.en: So there is a literature on protection from rhinovirus.
sentences.zh: 关于预防鼻病毒，确实有相关文献。

sentences.en: Rhinovirus, as you know, is a coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，鼻病毒是一种冠状病毒。

sentences.en: It's the common cold virus.
sentences.zh: 它是普通感冒病毒。

sentences.en: And Sheldon Cohen in Pittsburgh took a large number of volunteers, paid the meat $300, and put rhinoviruses in their nose, and then isolated them for two weeks.
sentences.zh: 匹兹堡的谢尔顿·科恩招募了大量志愿者，付给他们300美元，把鼻病毒滴进他们的鼻子里，然后将他们隔离了两周。

sentences.en: And asked, could he predict who would get a cold, and how severe it would be?
sentences.zh: 他想看看能否预测谁会感冒，以及感冒会有多严重。

sentences.en: And before they're isolated, he gives them a whole battery of tests, optimism, cheerfulness, positive emotion, negative emotion, and the like.
sentences.zh: 在隔离之前，他给他们做了一整套测试，包括乐观、开朗、积极情绪、消极情绪等。

sentences.en: The results are quite remarkable, and they're substantial.
sentences.zh: 结果非常显著，且影响巨大。

sentences.en: First, interesting to me, since I've spent my life working on optimism, optimism had no effect on whether or not you get a cold and how long it lasts.
sentences.zh: 首先，令我感兴趣的是，因为我毕生致力于研究乐观，结果发现乐观对你是否感冒以及感冒持续多久没有任何影响。

sentences.en: The big effect was being cheerful, merry, high, positive, effective, before the rhinovirus is put in the nose.
sentences.zh: 最大的影响因素是在鼻病毒进入鼻子之前，是否开朗、快乐、处于高积极情感状态。

sentences.en: Happy people, in the subjective well-being sense, got about half the colds, and they were shorter and less severe.
sentences.zh: 在主观幸福感意义上快乐的人，感冒几率降低了一半，而且病程更短、症状更轻。

sentences.en: And by the way, this was not about complaining, since he actually weighed the mucus.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，这与抱怨无关，因为他实际上称量了粘液。

sentences.en: So it was a rigorous measure of getting a cold.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个衡量感冒的严谨指标。

sentences.en: So the first lesson is, during the pandemic, if you're in a situation like mine, in which what you're trying to do for the next three months is just avoid getting it,
sentences.zh: 所以第一个教训是，在大流行期间，如果你像我一样，未来三个月的目标只是尽量避免感染，

sentences.en: in addition to wearing a mask and social distancing, you should have as much fun as you possibly can.
sentences.zh: 除了戴口罩和保持社交距离外，你应该尽可能多地找乐子。

sentences.en: Now, of course, it's difficult in a pandemic to have a lot of fun, but let me tell you my advice and what we've done.
sentences.zh: 当然，在大流行期间找乐子很难，但让我告诉你我的建议以及我们做了什么。

sentences.en: First, we bought a puppy, and the puppy brought us, until it's now 10 months old, enormous joy.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们买了一只小狗，直到现在它10个月大，这只小狗给我们带来了巨大的快乐。

sentences.en: Dancing, singing, sex, making love, good food, all the things that you can do in a pandemic and quarantine to have fun, even how difficult it is.
sentences.zh: 跳舞、唱歌、性生活、做爱、美食，所有你在大流行和隔离期间能做来找乐子的事，尽管这很难。

sentences.en: So I have Zoom sessions with my students, and we dance.
sentences.zh: 所以我通过Zoom和学生们开会，我们一起跳舞。

sentences.en: And a lot of the positive psychology website people have created COVID exercises to have fun.
sentences.zh: 许多积极心理学网站的人也创造了新冠期间的娱乐练习。

sentences.en: So that's part one.
sentences.zh: 这就是第一部分。

sentences.en: The science tells us, as hard as it is, have as much fun as you can.
sentences.zh: 科学告诉我们，尽管很难，但要尽可能多地找乐子。

sentences.en: And that may indeed be a protective factor.
sentences.zh: 那确实可能是一个保护因素。

sentences.en: Part two is the question, when this is over, and this too will pass, what characteristics matter?
sentences.zh: 第二部分是这个问题：当这一切结束时（这一切终将过去），哪些特征很重要？

sentences.en: Who recovers?
sentences.zh: 谁能恢复得更好？

sentences.en: Who is a better leader?
sentences.zh: 谁是更好的领导者？

sentences.en: Who is more productive?
sentences.zh: 谁的生产力更高？

sentences.en: And there, the data are that being cheerful and merry doesn't do anything at all.
sentences.zh: 数据表明，开朗和快乐在这些方面完全不起作用。

sentences.en: It's being optimistic and hopeful.
sentences.zh: 起作用的是乐观和希望。

sentences.en: It's the people who interpret the future as they're going to be good events, bad events are going to fade, bad events are only just this one situation,
sentences.zh: 是那些将未来解读为会有好事发生、坏事会消散、坏事只是当前这一种情况的人，

sentences.en: and I can do something about it.
sentences.zh: 并且认为我可以对此做些什么。

sentences.en: These are the people who go on to be more productive, healthier, and better leaders.
sentences.zh: 这些人往往更具生产力、更健康，也是更好的领导者。

sentences.en: So the bottom line here is, during the pandemic, have a great time as best you can.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的核心结论是：在大流行期间，尽你所能过得开心。

sentences.en: After the pandemic and as it ends, it's hope and optimism that are going to predict recovery, leadership, and our future.
sentences.zh: 在大流行之后及结束时，希望和乐观将决定恢复、领导力和我们的未来。

sentences.en: That leads me to wonder a little bit about, you might call it stickiness.
sentences.zh: 这让我有点好奇，你可以称之为“粘性”。

sentences.en: If people are not naturally optimistic, but they go through the actions of trying to behave in an optimistic way, does that measurably change their personality?
sentences.zh: 如果人们天生不乐观，但他们通过行动尝试以乐观的方式行事，这会从可测量的程度上改变他们的性格吗？

sentences.en: Can you learn to be optimistic if that's not your natural bent?
sentences.zh: 如果乐观不是你的天性，你能学会变得乐观吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I'm a good example of that.
sentences.zh: 我就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: So I'm naturally a depressive and a pessimist, and I take my own medicine, everything I'm about to say, I do, and my family does.
sentences.zh: 我天生是个抑郁症患者和悲观主义者，我服用自己的药方，我即将说的每一件事，我都在做，我的家人也在做。

sentences.en: So when we have a good idea about an intervention in positive psychology, I first do it on myself.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们对积极心理学的干预措施有了一个好的想法时，我首先会在自己身上试验。

sentences.en: If it works on me, I give it to my wife and seven children to do.
sentences.zh: 如果对我有效，我就让我的妻子和七个孩子去做。

sentences.en: If it works on them, I give it to my graduate students and postdocs, and we start to do outcome studies on it.
sentences.zh: 如果对他们有效，我就让我的研究生和博士后去做，我们开始对其进行结果研究。

sentences.en: So one thing that we have learned is that pessimism is changeable.
sentences.zh: 所以我们学到的一件事是，悲观是可以改变的。

sentences.en: You can change it to optimism.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它变成乐观。

sentences.en: And the key to this is first tuning in to the most pessimistic and the most catastrophic thoughts you say to yourself.
sentences.zh: 关键在于首先要意识到你对自己说的最悲观、最灾难性的想法。

sentences.en: And that's something people are pretty good at doing.
sentences.zh: 这是人们很擅长做的事情。

sentences.en: It's the main move in cognitive behavioral therapy.
sentences.zh: 这是认知行为疗法的主要步骤。

sentences.en: And then having identified your most catastrophic thoughts,
sentences.zh: 然后，在识别出你最灾难性的想法后，

sentences.en: treat them as if they were said to you by someone whose mission in life was to make you miserable and argue rationally against them.
sentences.zh: 把它们当作是一个人生目标就是让你痛苦的人对你说的，并理性地反驳它们。

sentences.en: So let me give you an example that I use and I've used during this pandemic.
sentences.zh: 让我给你一个我在这次大流行期间使用过的例子。

sentences.en: So my first thought when I came back home after 17 days of isolation was, you know, this medical stuff is nonsense.
sentences.zh: 所以，在隔离17天后回到家，我的第一个想法是：你知道，这些医疗建议都是胡扯。

sentences.en: They're still infectious.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然具有传染性。

sentences.en: I'm going to be down with this in four days.
sentences.zh: 四天内我就会倒下。

sentences.en: And I'm 78 years old, so I'm dead.
sentences.zh: 而且我已经78岁了，所以我死定了。

sentences.en: And the statistics are indeed that compared to the young population, I'm 222 times more likely to die.
sentences.zh: 统计数据确实显示，与年轻人相比，我死亡的可能性高出222倍。

sentences.en: So that's my first thought, my most catastrophic thought.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的第一个想法，我最灾难性的想法。

sentences.en: And then I argued against it rationally.
sentences.zh: 然后我理性地反驳了它。

sentences.en: So what I said to myself is called a put it in perspective exercise.
sentences.zh: 所以我对自己说的话被称为“换位思考练习”。

sentences.en: That says, first, go through the most catastrophic scenario possible.
sentences.zh: 它说，首先，经历可能发生的最灾难性的情景。

sentences.en: OK, I just did it.
sentences.zh: 好的，我刚刚做到了。

sentences.en: The second part is go through the least catastrophic.
sentences.zh: 第二部分是经历最不灾难性的情景。

sentences.en: What's the best thing that could happen?
sentences.zh: 可能发生的最好的事情是什么？

sentences.en: And so I said to myself, well, the best thing that can happen is they're not infectious.
sentences.zh: 所以我对自己说，嗯，最好的事情是他们没有传染性。

sentences.en: And indeed, these two wonderful vaccines are out.
sentences.zh: 而且确实，这两款很棒的疫苗已经出来了。

sentences.en: And I'm going to be just fine.
sentences.zh: 我会没事的。

sentences.en: And I'll get a vaccine first thing in January.
sentences.zh: 我会在一月份第一时间接种疫苗。

sentences.en: OK, then the third thing to do is having done the worst possible scenario and the best possible scenario.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么第三件事是，在做完了最坏的情况和最好的情况之后，

sentences.en: What's the most realistic scenario?
sentences.zh: 最现实的情况是什么？

sentences.en: Well, the most realistic scenario is I'm going to be very limited between now and the time a jab occurs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最现实的情况是，从现在到打上疫苗之前，我的活动会非常受限。

sentences.en: And I'm not going to get this in January.
sentences.zh: 而且我一月份打不上疫苗。

sentences.en: You know, the president and the vice president got it yesterday, but I'm not going to get it till the spring.
sentences.zh: 你知道，总统和副总统昨天打了，但我得等到春天才能打。

sentences.en: So what I have to do is plan for the future.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须为未来做计划。

sentences.en: I have to find a way to be at home most of the time to teach my classes and to minimize my exposure.
sentences.zh: 我必须找到一种方法，大部分时间待在家里教课，并尽量减少接触。

sentences.en: So the most likely scenario is the next three months are going to be difficult and there is a pretty good chance if I'm careful, I'll be able to avoid the infection.
sentences.zh: 所以最可能的情况是，接下来的三个月会很艰难，如果我小心谨慎，我有很大机会避免感染。

sentences.en: And that's that's not an infection.
sentences.zh: 那不是感染。

sentences.en: That's my early morning stuffiness.
sentences.zh: 那是我清晨的鼻塞。

sentences.en: The catastrophic interpretation would be, there it is.
sentences.zh: 灾难性的解读会是：看，就是它。

sentences.en: I've got COVID.
sentences.zh: 我得了新冠。

sentences.en: The most realistic explanation is early morning stuffiness.
sentences.zh: 最现实的解释是清晨鼻塞。

sentences.en: That's a good exercise that any one of our listeners could do and could benefit from.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的练习，我们任何听众都可以做，并从中受益。

sentences.en: Let me change gears and talk a little bit about the effects of the pandemic on children and how disruptions to school and socializing and other life experiences may affect them in the long run.
sentences.zh: 让我换个话题，谈谈大流行对儿童的影响，以及学校和社交的中断以及其他生活经历在长期内可能如何影响他们。

sentences.en: What kind of advice might you have for parents, educators or others on how to help children's well-being right now?
sentences.zh: 对于家长、教育工作者或其他关心儿童福祉的人，你现在有什么建议吗？

sentences.en: What can we do to help make them more optimistic?
sentences.zh: 我们能做些什么来帮助他们变得更乐观？

sentences.en: Well, the same things work with children as working with adults, and that is recognizing catastrophic thoughts and disputing them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对成年人有效的方法对孩子同样有效，那就是识别灾难性想法并反驳它们。

sentences.en: But there's no doubt that a year away from school and away from friends is going to make things more difficult.
sentences.zh: 但毫无疑问，离开学校和朋友一年会让事情变得更困难。

sentences.en: And so there, it's optimism that's going to matter and what we do when we come out of a pandemic.
sentences.zh: 所以，乐观精神很重要，我们在走出大流行时所做的事情也很重要。

sentences.en: But I think I want to say something general, Kim, about my view of the future, given the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我想说一些普遍的看法，金，关于我对未来的看法，鉴于这次大流行。

sentences.en: I think the world is in labor and something is being born and that we will learn from this pandemic what to keep and what to throw away.
sentences.zh: 我认为世界正在阵痛中，有什么东西正在诞生，我们将从这次大流行中学会保留什么，抛弃什么。

sentences.en: But importantly, there are two views of children and our future, given this pandemic.
sentences.zh: 但重要的是，鉴于这次大流行，对于儿童和我们的未来有两种观点。

sentences.en: I'm going to call it Yates versus Juliana.
sentences.zh: 我称之为叶芝（Yates）与朱利安（Juliana）之争。

sentences.en: Yates, 100 years ago, in his poem about the troubled, asked, what rough beast is slouching its way to Bethlehem now to be born?
sentences.zh: 叶芝在100年前关于困境的诗中问道：现在有什么粗野的野兽正蹒跚着向伯利恒走去，等待出生？

sentences.en: This is the pessimistic view that the labor that the world is in now is going to result in something worse than what we have.
sentences.zh: 这是一种悲观的观点，认为世界目前所处的阵痛将导致比我们现在拥有的更糟糕的结果。

sentences.en: So the Yates view, highly pessimistic.
sentences.zh: 所以叶芝的观点是非常悲观的。

sentences.en: And all you need to do is pick up the New York Times to hear the Yates view one way or another.
sentences.zh: 你只需要拿起《纽约时报》，就能以某种方式听到叶芝的观点。

sentences.en: Juliana of Norwich is the one I lean to.
sentences.zh: 我倾向于诺里奇的朱利安。

sentences.en: Juliana, as you may remember, was a monk.
sentences.zh: 你可能记得，朱利安是一位僧侣。

sentences.en: You had to take a male name to be a monk.
sentences.zh: 你必须取一个男性名字才能成为僧侣。

sentences.en: She's called Julian of Norwich.
sentences.zh: 她被称为诺里奇的朱利安。

sentences.en: And she wrote, in the middle of the Black Plague, and by the way, the Black Plague is 100 times worse than what we're going through now.
sentences.zh: 她在黑死病期间写道，顺便说一下，黑死病比我们现在经历的要严重100倍。

sentences.en: Humans have gone through plagues for time immemorial.
sentences.zh: 人类自古以来就经历过瘟疫。

sentences.en: The Black Plague killed one third of the European population.
sentences.zh: 黑死病杀死了欧洲三分之一的人口。

sentences.en: And there was no safety net at all.
sentences.zh: 而且根本没有任何安全网。

sentences.en: There was no zooming.
sentences.zh: 没有Zoom。

sentences.en: And it was, in many ways, the worst of times.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，那是至暗时刻。

sentences.en: And Juliana, a Neoplatonist mystic, wrote the following about what was being born.
sentences.zh: 而朱利安，一位新柏拉图主义神秘主义者，写下了关于正在诞生的事物的以下内容。

sentences.en: He said not, thou shalt not be travailed.
sentences.zh: 他说，并非你不会受苦。

sentences.en: He said not, thou shalt not be tempestive.
sentences.zh: 他说，并非你不会经历风暴。

sentences.en: He said not, thou shalt not be diseased.
sentences.zh: 他说，不要怕，你不会被疾病所困。

sentences.en: He said, thou shalt not be overcome.
sentences.zh: 他说，不要怕，你不会被击倒。

sentences.en: And all shall be well.
sentences.zh: 一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: And all shall be well.
sentences.zh: 一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: And all manner of things shall be well.
sentences.zh: 一切事物都会好起来的。

sentences.en: This is the dilemma we're in now about our future.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们现在面临的关于未来的困境。

sentences.en: Will there be a beast slouching its way to Bethlehem to be born to take over the world?
sentences.zh: 是否会有某种野兽正蹒跚走向伯利恒，降生并接管这个世界？

sentences.en: Or will all things be well?
sentences.zh: 还是说一切都会好起来？

sentences.en: And for me, the Juliana view is, and the Yates view are both self-fulfilling.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，朱莉安娜的观点和耶茨的观点都是自我实现的预言。

sentences.en: So what we need here is optimism, planning, and hope for the future.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在需要的是乐观、规划以及对未来的希望。

sentences.en: Let's talk for a moment about some of your earliest research into learned helplessness.
sentences.zh: 让我们谈谈你早期关于习得性无助的一些研究。

sentences.en: You studied dogs and other mammals.
sentences.zh: 你研究过狗和其他哺乳动物。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering how, in the intervening years, you've changed your thinking around learned helplessness.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，在随后的这些年里，你对习得性无助的看法发生了怎样的改变。

sentences.en: And now you talk more about the idea of learned hopefulness.
sentences.zh: 现在你更多地谈论习得性希望的概念。

sentences.en: Can you explain for our listeners first what is meant by learned helplessness, which they might not be familiar with?
sentences.zh: 你能先为我们的听众解释一下什么是习得性无助吗？他们可能不太熟悉这个概念。

sentences.en: And then tell us how and why your thinking and research in this area evolved.
sentences.zh: 然后再告诉我们，你在这个领域的思考和研究是如何演变的，以及为什么会演变。

sentences.en: Yes, learned helplessness has been slipped on its head in the last 20 years.
sentences.zh: 是的，在过去20年里，习得性无助的概念被彻底颠覆了。

sentences.en: So, 50 years ago, Steve Mayer and Bruce Overmeyer and I found that when animals and people experience bad events that they couldn't do anything about,
sentences.zh: 50年前，史蒂夫·迈耶、布鲁斯·奥弗迈耶和我发现，当动物和人类经历无法改变的糟糕事件时，

sentences.en: that they collapsed and became passive and became helpless.
sentences.zh: 他们会崩溃、变得消极并陷入无助。

sentences.en: And we called it learned helplessness.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为习得性无助。

sentences.en: And what we found, that people and animals who got the very same events, but they could do something about them, did not become helpless.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，那些经历了同样事件但能够采取行动去改变的人和动物，并没有变得无助。

sentences.en: Well, Steve Mayer went off and became a neuroscientiSt.
sentences.zh: 后来，史蒂夫·迈耶去做了神经科学家。

sentences.en: And starting around 1990, 1995, we began to get pretty good tools for looking at the brain.
sentences.zh: 从1990年、1995年左右开始，我们开始拥有了相当不错的脑部观察工具。

sentences.en: And Steve wanted to know what was happening in the brain of rats when they became helpless.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫想知道大鼠在变得无助时，大脑中发生了什么。

sentences.en: And the findings were astonishing.
sentences.zh: 研究结果令人震惊。

sentences.en: And they flipped the field on its head.
sentences.zh: 它们彻底颠覆了这个领域。

sentences.en: But what Steve found is that both in animals and human, there's a structure sort of up the nose.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫发现，无论是在动物还是人类身上，鼻腔上方都有一个结构。

sentences.en: It's 50,000 cells in a rat and 150,000 cells in a human called the dorsorephane nucleus.
sentences.zh: 在大鼠身上有5万个细胞，在人类身上有15万个细胞，被称为背侧中缝核。

sentences.en: And the dorsorephane nucleus, its activity produces helplessness.
sentences.zh: 而背侧中缝核的活动会产生无助感。

sentences.en: It's necessary and sufficient for producing helplessness.
sentences.zh: 它是产生无助感的必要且充分条件。

sentences.en: Now, very interesting, it turns out there is a circuit from up here in the forebrain, the medial frontal lobes.
sentences.zh: 非常有趣的是，大脑前部，即内侧额叶，存在一条回路。

sentences.en: There's a specific circuit that goes down to the dorsorephane nucleus and turns it off.
sentences.zh: 有一条特定的回路通向背侧中缝核并将其关闭。

sentences.en: And it turns it off when you learn mastery, when you have hope.
sentences.zh: 当你学会掌控、当你拥有希望时，它就会将其关闭。

sentences.en: So, it turns out that contrary to what we thought 50 years ago, and this is one of the great things about being in a science for 50 years, you can find out you're wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以事实证明，与我们50年前的想法相反——这也是从事科学研究50年的伟大之处，你可以发现自己错了。

sentences.en: We found out we were wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们发现我们错了。

sentences.en: Being helpless is the default mammalian reaction to troubles.
sentences.zh: 无助是哺乳动物面对困难时的默认反应。

sentences.en: We're born helpless.
sentences.zh: 我们生来就是无助的。

sentences.en: The default reaction is to give up.
sentences.zh: 默认反应就是放弃。

sentences.en: What we have, however, what humans have is a circuit, which I call the hope circuit, which, when it's ignited by mastery and hope, turns off helplessness.
sentences.zh: 然而，人类拥有一种回路，我称之为希望回路，当它被掌控感和希望点燃时，就会关闭无助感。

sentences.en: So, it turns out what's learned in helplessness experiments is hope and mastery, and that's the protective factor.
sentences.zh: 所以，习得性无助实验中真正习得的是希望和掌控感，这才是保护因素。

sentences.en: So, it's a great story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很棒的故事。

sentences.en: And there was a lead article in the Psych Review a couple of years ago, which tells the whole story.
sentences.zh: 几年前《心理学评论》上的一篇主打文章讲述了整个故事。

sentences.en: And it's told in my book, The Hope Circuit.
sentences.zh: 我的书《希望回路》中也讲述了它。

sentences.en: That's why I called it The Hope Circuit.
sentences.zh: 这就是我把它命名为《希望回路》的原因。

sentences.en: You've described several eureka moments in your life that has led you to change the direction of your thinking and your research.
sentences.zh: 你曾描述过生命中几个让你改变思考和研究方向的顿悟时刻。

sentences.en: One happened many years ago when you were gardening with your daughter, who was then five years old.
sentences.zh: 其中一个发生在多年前，你和当时五岁的女儿在花园里干活时。

sentences.en: And another came when you had an extraordinary dream that involved the Guggenheim Museum and a sort of celestial message you received.
sentences.zh: 另一个则源于你做的一个非凡的梦，梦里涉及古根海姆博物馆和你收到的一种天启信息。

sentences.en: Could you talk about those incidents and how they influenced your work and your life?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这些事件以及它们如何影响了你的工作和生活吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I've been the fortunate recipient of at least two life-changing epiphanies.
sentences.zh: 是的，我有幸获得了至少两次改变人生的顿悟。

sentences.en: One occurred in what is called a numinous dream.
sentences.zh: 一次发生在一个被称为神圣的梦中。

sentences.en: And the other occurred in my garden right after I had been elected president of the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 另一次发生在我当选美国心理学会主席后不久，在我的花园里。

sentences.en: So, I'll narrate each of them, Kim.
sentences.zh: 那么，金，我来一一讲述。

sentences.en: The dream one occurred about two weeks after quite an extraordinary lunch with my mentor, Aaron Beck.
sentences.zh: 那个梦发生在我和导师亚伦·贝克进行了一次非凡的午餐大约两周后。

sentences.en: Tim is now 99 and a half years old.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆现在已经99岁半了。

sentences.en: He and I still meet once a week.
sentences.zh: 我和他仍然每周见一次面。

sentences.en: He's in great shape mentally.
sentences.zh: 他的精神状态非常好。

sentences.en: And back then, this is now almost 50 years ago, we would have lunch once a week.
sentences.zh: 那时，也就是将近50年前，我们每周会一起吃午饭。

sentences.en: And he's a very kindly, gentle soul.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常善良、温柔的人。

sentences.en: And 50 years ago, I was a tenured professor at Penn doing animal experimental psychology.
sentences.zh: 50年前，我是宾夕法尼亚大学的终身教授，从事动物实验心理学研究。

sentences.en: And over lunch, Tim said, Marty, if you continue to do what you're doing, you're going to waste your life.
sentences.zh: 午餐时，蒂姆说：“马蒂，如果你继续做你现在做的事，你就是在浪费生命。”

sentences.en: And I kind of choked on my grilled Reuben and took it under advisement.
sentences.zh: 我当时差点被鲁宾三明治噎住，并把这话记在了心里。

sentences.en: And about two weeks later, I had the following dream.
sentences.zh: 大约两周后，我做了下面这个梦。

sentences.en: In this dream, and dreaming is something I've worked on much of my life.
sentences.zh: 在这个梦里——梦是我一生中研究过很多的东西。

sentences.en: And in fact, I think the best paper I ever wrote, which no one has read, is called What is a Dream?
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为我写过的最好的论文，虽然没人读过，叫作《什么是梦？》。

sentences.en: And for me, this nails the process of what dreaming is.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这抓住了梦的过程。

sentences.en: But without going through the theory of dreaming, here was the dream.
sentences.zh: 但就不深入探讨梦的理论了，梦的内容是这样的：

sentences.en: I'm walking up the ramp at the Guggenheim Museum.
sentences.zh: 我正走在古根海姆博物馆的坡道上。

sentences.en: And I noticed that on the right, there are doors.
sentences.zh: 我注意到右边有几扇门。

sentences.en: And I open each of the doors, and there are people playing with cards.
sentences.zh: 我打开每一扇门，里面都有人在玩牌。

sentences.en: And I'm very puzzled about this.
sentences.zh: 我对此感到非常困惑。

sentences.en: So I asked the question, why is everyone playing with cards?
sentences.zh: 所以我问了一个问题：为什么每个人都在玩牌？

sentences.en: Whereupon, the roof of the Guggenheim opens, and the Godhead appears.
sentences.zh: 随即，古根海姆的屋顶打开了，上帝显现了。

sentences.en: And God, Kim, you'll be happy to hear, is an elderly male.
sentences.zh: 金，你听到这个会很高兴，上帝是一位年长的男性。

sentences.en: Look, white beard.
sentences.zh: 看，白胡子。

sentences.en: Gray, with a booming voice.
sentences.zh: 灰色的，声音洪亮。

sentences.en: And God says to me, Seligman, at least you're starting to ask the right questions.
sentences.zh: 上帝对我说：“塞利格曼，至少你开始问正确的问题了。”

sentences.en: And that changed my life, actually.
sentences.zh: 这确实改变了我的生活。

sentences.en: So it's what moved me from being an experimental psychologist to a clinical psychologist, from an experimental researcher to a longitudinal researcher, and from animals to humans.
sentences.zh: 正是它让我从一名实验心理学家转变为临床心理学家，从实验研究者转变为纵向研究者，并从研究动物转向研究人类。

sentences.en: So it was a dream that moved me and has stayed with me.
sentences.zh: 所以是一个梦改变了我，并一直伴随着我。

sentences.en: Fast forward now 30 years.
sentences.zh: 现在快进30年。

sentences.en: I'm elected president of the American Psychological Association, and I'm told that presidents are supposed to have initiatives.
sentences.zh: 我当选为美国心理学会主席，有人告诉我主席应该有自己的倡议。

sentences.en: And I didn't really know what mine was going to be.
sentences.zh: 我当时真的不知道我的倡议会是什么。

sentences.en: I've worked in a lot of different areas.
sentences.zh: 我在很多不同的领域工作过。

sentences.en: And as I was mulling this, taking office, I was in my garden.
sentences.zh: 当我在考虑这个问题并准备上任时，我正在花园里。

sentences.en: I'm a gardener.
sentences.zh: 我是一个园丁。

sentences.en: And with my five-year-old daughter, Nikki.
sentences.zh: 当时我五岁的女儿尼基也在。

sentences.en: Nikki is now a clinical psychologist, by the way, getting her PhD from Fordham, doing her internship.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，尼基现在是一位临床心理学家，正在福特汉姆大学攻读博士学位，并进行实习。

sentences.en: But she founded positive psychology in the following way.
sentences.zh: 但她是以以下方式创立了积极心理学。

sentences.en: She had just had her fifth birthday, about maybe two weeks before this incident in the garden.
sentences.zh: 她刚过完五岁生日，大约是在花园里发生这件事的两周前。

sentences.en: And we're in the garden together, and I'm weeding.
sentences.zh: 我们在一起除草。

sentences.en: And Nikki is having a great time.
sentences.zh: 尼基玩得很开心。

sentences.en: She's singing and dancing and throwing weeds in the air.
sentences.zh: 她又唱又跳，把杂草扔向空中。

sentences.en: And I yelled at her, and I said, get to work, Nikki, damn it.
sentences.zh: 我冲她大喊：“快干活，尼基，该死的。”

sentences.en: We're weeding.
sentences.zh: 我们在除草。

sentences.en: And Nikki walks away, and she comes back.
sentences.zh: 尼基走开了，然后又回来了。

sentences.en: She says, Daddy, can I talk to you?
sentences.zh: 她说：“爸爸，我能跟你谈谈吗？”

sentences.en: And I said, sure, Nikki, what is it?
sentences.zh: 我说：“当然可以，尼基，什么事？”

sentences.en: She said, Daddy, have you noticed?
sentences.zh: 她说：“爸爸，你注意到了吗？”

sentences.en: I used to be a whiner.
sentences.zh: “我以前是个爱抱怨的孩子。”

sentences.en: And have you noticed that since my fifth birthday, I haven't whined once?
sentences.zh: “你注意到从我五岁生日那天起，我就再没抱怨过一次了吗？”

sentences.en: And I said, oh, yeah, yeah, Nikki, that's right.
sentences.zh: 我说：“哦，是的，是的，尼基，没错。”

sentences.en: He said, well, Daddy, on my fifth birthday, I decided that I wasn't going to whine anymore.
sentences.zh: 她说：“嗯，爸爸，在我五岁生日那天，我决定不再抱怨了。”

sentences.en: And that was the hardest thing I've ever done.
sentences.zh: “那是我做过的最难的事情。”

sentences.en: And if I can stop whining, you can stop being such a grouch.
sentences.zh: “如果我能停止抱怨，你也能停止做一个脾气暴躁的人。”

sentences.en: And she hit the nail on the head in three different ways.
sentences.zh: 她一针见血地指出了三个方面的问题。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, I realized three different things.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，我意识到了三件事。

sentences.en: First, that she was right, and that I was a grouch.
sentences.zh: 首先，她是对的，我确实是个脾气暴躁的人。

sentences.en: And indeed, what I thought, what I was so proud about was my ability to see what was wrong with everything.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我曾经引以为傲的，正是能看出每件事哪里出了问题的能力。

sentences.en: And I realized for the first time, maybe any success I had in life was not because of being a pessimist and a grouch and a critic.
sentences.zh: 我第一次意识到，我生命中取得的任何成功，可能并不是因为我是一个悲观主义者、一个暴躁的人和一个批评家。

sentences.en: But maybe it was because I could sometimes see what was right rather than what was wrong.
sentences.zh: 而是因为我有时能看到什么是对的，而不是什么是错的。

sentences.en: And I decided to change.
sentences.zh: 我决定改变。

sentences.en: And indeed, I have.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我也确实做到了。

sentences.en: I measure these things, not only in the general population, but in myself.
sentences.zh: 我不只在普通人群中衡量这些，也在我自己身上衡量。

sentences.en: So the first thing was Nikki was right, and I was a grouch.
sentences.zh: 所以第一点是尼基是对的，而我确实是个暴躁的人。

sentences.en: And maybe being a grouch really got in the way of doing what I wanted in life.
sentences.zh: 也许这种暴躁真的阻碍了我去实现生命中想要做的事情。

sentences.en: And the second thing I realized was that my theory of child rearing was wrong.
sentences.zh: 第二点我意识到的是，我的育儿理论错了。

sentences.en: So my theory of child rearing in education was remedial.
sentences.zh: 我的教育和育儿理论是补救性的。

sentences.en: It basically said that what our job as teachers and parents to do was to find out what our kids were doing wrong and correct them.
sentences.zh: 它基本上认为，作为老师和父母，我们的工作是找出孩子们做错的地方并纠正他们。

sentences.en: And somehow, if we corrected all of their errors, we'd get an exemplary child.
sentences.zh: 如果能纠正他们所有的错误，我们就能得到一个模范孩子。

sentences.en: Well, it struck me that that's nonsense.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我突然觉得这简直是胡说八道。

sentences.en: What you get then is a child that's not doing anything wrong.
sentences.zh: 那样你得到的只是一个什么错都不犯的孩子。

sentences.en: But your job as a parent and a teacher is to find out what the kid does right, what they're strong at.
sentences.zh: 但作为父母和老师，你的工作是找出孩子做得对的地方，他们的长处是什么。

sentences.en: And what I saw in Nikki now was her ability to talk sense to adults and to identify that strength
sentences.zh: 我现在在尼基身上看到的是她与成年人讲道理的能力，并识别出那种优势，

sentences.en: and to get your child or your student to live their life around what they do well, not to spend their life avoiding what they do badly.
sentences.zh: 让你的孩子或学生围绕他们擅长的事情去生活，而不是花一生去避免他们不擅长的事情。

sentences.en: So that was the second thing I learned.
sentences.zh: 这就是我学到的第二件事。

sentences.en: And I changed my child rearing and my teaching.
sentences.zh: 我改变了我的育儿和教学方式。

sentences.en: My teaching used to be all full of red marks on papers.
sentences.zh: 我以前的教学作业上全是红色的批改标记。

sentences.en: And now it's full of blue marks, which says, hey, that's a really perfect sentence.
sentences.zh: 而现在全是蓝色的标记，上面写着：嘿，那是一个非常完美的句子。

sentences.en: You got that word exactly right.
sentences.zh: 你把那个词用得非常准确。

sentences.en: And the third thing I realized was about psychology, about APA, for that matter,
sentences.zh: 第三点我意识到的是关于心理学，关于美国心理学会，

sentences.en: that psychology had been all about what was wrong, pathology, weakness, the things that were going wrong in the world.
sentences.zh: 心理学一直以来关注的都是哪里出了问题、病理、弱点，以及世界上正在变糟的事情。

sentences.en: Indeed, I had worked on that for 30 years, depression, schizophrenia, drug addiction, suicide, and the like.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我已经在那个领域工作了30年，抑郁症、精神分裂症、药物成瘾、自杀等等。

sentences.en: But that's only half the battle.
sentences.zh: 但这只是战斗的一半。

sentences.en: The other half of the battle is recognizing what's going well in life and building it and leading your life around it.
sentences.zh: 战斗的另一半是认识到生活中什么是顺利的，并去建立它，围绕它来生活。

sentences.en: So it occurred to me in that epiphany that there could be a movement, positive psychology,
sentences.zh: 所以在那次顿悟中，我想到可以有一场运动，即积极心理学，

sentences.en: whose mission in life would be to recognize not just the troubles and do something about it,
sentences.zh: 其使命不仅是识别困难并解决问题，

sentences.en: not just what cripples life, but what makes life worth living and teaches people the skills that make life worth living.
sentences.zh: 不仅是关注那些摧毁生活的事物，还要关注是什么让生活值得过，并教给人们让生活值得过的技能。

sentences.en: From that, I think you've distilled your research into positive psychology into something that you call the PERMA model.
sentences.zh: 由此看来，你已经将你对积极心理学的研究提炼成了你所说的PERMA模型。

sentences.en: What is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: So once you decide that you want to work on well-being and you want to work on what enables a good life, as opposed to what cripples life, you essentially need the opposite of DSM.
sentences.zh: 一旦你决定要致力于幸福感，致力于研究什么能成就美好的生活，而不是什么会摧毁生活，你本质上就需要一个与DSM（精神疾病诊断与统计手册）相反的东西。

sentences.en: You need a definition of the sanities, not just the definition of the crazinesses.
sentences.zh: 你需要一个关于健康的定义，而不仅仅是关于疯狂的定义。

sentences.en: And so what are the elements, what are the pillars of a good life?
sentences.zh: 那么，美好生活的要素是什么，支柱是什么？

sentences.en: And PERMA says there are five of them.
sentences.zh: PERMA说有五个要素。

sentences.en: There are five things that non-suffering free people choose.
sentences.zh: 有五件事是无痛苦的自由人会选择的。

sentences.en: The first is P, positive emotion, being happy, feeling good, high subjective well-being.
sentences.zh: 第一个是P，积极情绪，快乐，感觉良好，高主观幸福感。

sentences.en: The second is E, engagement, being one with the music, being completely wrapped up in your work or with someone you love.
sentences.zh: 第二个是E，投入，与音乐合而为一，完全沉浸在你的工作中或与你所爱的人在一起。

sentences.en: And it's always my hope when I'm lecturing that the people who are listening to this are at E.
sentences.zh: 我每次演讲时都希望听众们正处于E的状态。

sentences.en: They're completely engaged.
sentences.zh: 他们完全投入其中。

sentences.en: We find, by the way, that about 60% of you are in E right now.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，我们发现你们中大约60%的人现在正处于E的状态。

sentences.en: The other 40% of you are having sexual fantasies.
sentences.zh: 剩下的40%正在进行性幻想。

sentences.en: Or no, that's okay, I guess.
sentences.zh: 或者不，没关系，我想。

sentences.en: R, P-E-R, is good relationships.
sentences.zh: R，P-E-R，是良好的人际关系。

sentences.en: So people pursue relationships.
sentences.zh: 所以人们追求人际关系。

sentences.en: We're not only individuals, but we're hive creatures.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅是个体，我们还是群居生物。

sentences.en: We're like the bees and the wasps and the termites.
sentences.zh: 我们就像蜜蜂、黄蜂和白蚁一样。

sentences.en: We want to be part of something.
sentences.zh: 我们想要成为某个整体的一部分。

sentences.en: And that leads to M, which is meaning in life.
sentences.zh: 这引出了M，即生活中的意义（Meaning）。

sentences.en: And that's meaning and purpose.
sentences.zh: 也就是意义和目标。

sentences.en: Latching on to something that you believe in that's larger than you, that you can belong to and serve.
sentences.zh: 坚持某种你所信仰的、比你自身更宏大的事物，你可以归属于它并为之服务。

sentences.en: That's what meaning is.
sentences.zh: 这就是意义所在。

sentences.en: And finally, there's A, achievement, accomplishment, mastery, and competence.
sentences.zh: 最后是A，成就（Achievement）、完成、精通和能力。

sentences.en: So for me, the ingredients of a positive life come down to a dashboard of PERMA.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，积极生活的要素归结为PERMA这个仪表盘。

sentences.en: How much positive emotion?
sentences.zh: 有多少积极情绪？

sentences.en: How much engagement?
sentences.zh: 有多少投入度？

sentences.en: How good are your relationships?
sentences.zh: 你的人际关系有多好？

sentences.en: How much meaning do you have in life?
sentences.zh: 你的生活中有多少意义？

sentences.en: And how much accomplishment do you have in life?
sentences.zh: 你的生活中又有多少成就感？

sentences.en: Those are the five elements of positive psychology for me.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，这就是积极心理学的五个要素。

sentences.en: Over the past year or so, I've talked to several psychologists on this podcast about how the pandemic has been a giant natural experiment for them.
sentences.zh: 在过去一年左右的时间里，我在这个播客中与几位心理学家谈论了疫情对他们来说是如何成为一场巨大的自然实验的。

sentences.en: It's led to research in areas as varied as telework, boredom, ritual, things like that.
sentences.zh: 它促成了远程办公、无聊感、仪式感等各个领域的研究。

sentences.en: I noticed on the Penn Positive Psychology Center website that there's a link to a COVID-19 study.
sentences.zh: 我注意到宾夕法尼亚大学积极心理学中心的网站上有一个关于COVID-19研究的链接。

sentences.en: What are you looking at and what are you hoping to learn?
sentences.zh: 你们在关注什么，希望了解什么？

sentences.en: Well, I'm not sure what you're referring to here, Kim.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不确定你指的是什么，Kim。

sentences.en: So we have a website called AuthenticHappiness.org.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个名为AuthenticHappiness.org的网站。

sentences.en: And about 2,000 people, new people a day, come to it and they take the tests on it.
sentences.zh: 每天大约有2000名新用户访问并进行测试。

sentences.en: So we have, across the whole pandemic, a naturally occurring experiment in which we're able to look at increases and decreases in well-being and strengths.
sentences.zh: 因此，在整个疫情期间，我们拥有一个自然发生的实验，能够观察幸福感和优势的增长与下降。

sentences.en: In depression and anxiety.
sentences.zh: 以及抑郁和焦虑的情况。

sentences.en: And so we will eventually try to put this all together, very large groups of people, and ask the question about the course of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 所以我们最终会尝试将这些庞大群体的数据汇总起来，探讨疫情的发展历程。

sentences.en: And this allows us to predict things like who gets infection, who recovers rapidly and the like.
sentences.zh: 这使我们能够预测谁会感染、谁会迅速康复等情况。

sentences.en: But I'm not ready to discuss any data yet at this point.
sentences.zh: 但我目前还没准备好讨论任何数据。

sentences.en: Sure, yeah, we're still in the middle of this, so.
sentences.zh: 当然，是的，我们还处于疫情之中，所以。

sentences.en: Yeah, but we've got a very good database.
sentences.zh: 是的，但我们有一个非常好的数据库。

sentences.en: And this is something you were looking at anyway.
sentences.zh: 而且这本来就是你一直在关注的事情。

sentences.en: And now, because of the pandemic, you're seeing that you're going to be asking, evaluating.
sentences.zh: 现在，因为疫情，你发现你将要进行询问和评估。

sentences.en: We look at it all the time.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在关注它。

sentences.en: So, for example, this was going on before 9-11.
sentences.zh: 例如，这在9-11事件之前就已经开始了。

sentences.en: And so we had hundreds of people at that time, now thousands, coming every day.
sentences.zh: 当时我们有数百人，现在有数千人，每天都会来。

sentences.en: And what we found after 9-11, we looked for the next three months at changes in the strengths.
sentences.zh: 我们在9-11事件后发现，我们在接下来的三个月里观察了优势的变化。

sentences.en: And what we found in the United States was that hope, love, and faith increased forgiveness over the next three months in America, but not in any other country.
sentences.zh: 我们在美国发现，希望、爱和信仰在接下来的三个月里增加了宽容度，但在其他国家却没有。

sentences.en: And then by about three months later, that had gone back to baseline.
sentences.zh: 大约三个月后，这些指标又回到了基准水平。

sentences.en: So, events like 9-11, and we haven't yet looked for the pandemic, actually increase strengths like hope and love.
sentences.zh: 所以，像9-11这样的事件——我们还没有研究疫情——实际上增加了希望和爱这样的优势。

sentences.en: But the increases don't necessarily endure, apparently.
sentences.zh: 但显然，这种增长并不一定会持续。

sentences.en: And they don't laSt.
sentences.zh: 它们不会持久。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that's very, very large numbers of people.
sentences.zh: 而且这是基于非常非常庞大的人群。

sentences.en: So, these are pretty reliable statistics.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些统计数据相当可靠。

sentences.en: So, we've, for more than 20 years now, been mapping the world or the English-speaking world that comes every day to the website and takes questionnaires.
sentences.zh: 二十多年来，我们一直在对世界，或者说每天访问网站并填写问卷的英语世界进行测绘。

sentences.en: Changing gears a little bit, positive psychology has become accepted within the discipline over the last several decades, but it's also inspired some pushback.
sentences.zh: 换个话题，积极心理学在过去几十年里已被该学科所接受，但也引发了一些抵制。

sentences.en: Where I work at APA, we answer a lot of calls from reporters.
sentences.zh: 我在美国心理学会（APA）工作，我们经常接到记者的电话。

sentences.en: And recently, we fielded a number on toxic positivity, the idea that feeling forced to try to be happy and positive all the time can actually be bad for our well-being.
sentences.zh: 最近，我们处理了许多关于“有毒积极性”的咨询，即那种被迫时刻保持快乐和积极的想法，实际上可能对我们的幸福感有害。

sentences.en: What are your thoughts on this?
sentences.zh: 你对此有什么看法？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think trying to force anyone to do something is bad for our well-being.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为强迫任何人做任何事都对我们的幸福感有害。

sentences.en: And so, trying to force people to be positive can be toxic.
sentences.zh: 所以，强迫人们保持积极可能是“有毒”的。

sentences.en: So, one has to weigh the consequences of becoming more positive.
sentences.zh: 因此，一个人必须权衡变得更积极的后果。

sentences.en: That is, of going through the work of disputing your most pessimistic thoughts, which is not easy, particularly during a pandemic, against its benefits,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，在经历反驳你最悲观想法的过程中——这并不容易，尤其是在疫情期间——与它的益处之间进行权衡，

sentences.en: which are things like re-employment, recovery, and resilience.
sentences.zh: 这些益处包括重新就业、康复和韧性等。

sentences.en: So, people who adopt optimism and good cheer naturally are very lucky.
sentences.zh: 所以，那些自然而然地采取乐观和愉快态度的人是非常幸运的。

sentences.en: People like me, who have to learn optimism, run into the danger of, well, this is a task and this is difficult.
sentences.zh: 像我这样必须学习乐观的人，会面临这样的危险：好吧，这是一项任务，而且很困难。

sentences.en: And there's a literature on this.
sentences.zh: 而且这方面有相关的文献。

sentences.en: And so, for example, one of the reliable exercises in positive psychology is to do acts of kindness for other people.
sentences.zh: 例如，积极心理学中可靠的练习之一就是为他人做善事。

sentences.en: And indeed, we find that if you're assigned to do a random act of kindness next Wednesday, and you do it, your depression goes down and your life satisfaction goes up.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们发现如果你被安排在下周三做一件随机的善事，并且你做了，你的抑郁感会下降，生活满意度会上升。

sentences.en: But if you're assigned to do it every day, then you get the reverse effect.
sentences.zh: 但如果你被安排每天都做，那么效果就会适得其反。

sentences.en: So, you have to find a way not to overtax people.
sentences.zh: 所以，你必须找到一种不让人们负担过重的方法。

sentences.en: And so, that's my reaction to the notion.
sentences.zh: 这就是我对这个概念的反应。

sentences.en: But on the whole, I think the benefits of learning optimism and learning PERMA quite outweigh the drawbacks.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，我认为学习乐观和学习PERMA的益处远大于弊端。

sentences.en: But it's a clinical skill, and you have to do it with a light touch and at the right time, and you can't overdo it.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种临床技能，你必须以轻柔的方式、在合适的时机进行，而且不能过度。

sentences.en: Another criticism I've seen is that positive psychology puts the onus for human flourishing too much on the individual,
sentences.zh: 我看到的另一个批评是，积极心理学将人类繁荣的责任过多地归咎于个人，

sentences.en: and that it takes attention away from some of the societal factors, such as racism and poverty, that limit people's ability to live a meaningful life.
sentences.zh: 并且它转移了对一些社会因素的关注，例如种族主义和贫困，这些因素限制了人们过上有意义生活的能力。

sentences.en: Is that a legitimate critique?
sentences.zh: 这是一个合理的批评吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, this is a very important kind of question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个非常重要的问题。

sentences.en: And legitimate is the wrong word, but here's the way I think about it.
sentences.zh: “合理”这个词可能不太准确，但我是这样想的。

sentences.en: If you're interested in the world and you want a better world, what is the right balance between building individual happiness and building a collective happiness in the world?
sentences.zh: 如果你关心这个世界，并且想要一个更美好的世界，那么在建立个人幸福和建立集体幸福之间，什么是正确的平衡？

sentences.en: And these are often in tension with one another.
sentences.zh: 这两者往往处于紧张关系中。

sentences.en: And so, for example, I just gave a lecture to Nordic young students on this issue.
sentences.zh: 例如，我刚就这个问题给北欧的年轻学生做了一场讲座。

sentences.en: And many of them want to become politicians and change the basic things that are wrong with Nordic government.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人想成为政治家，改变北欧政府中存在的基本问题。

sentences.en: And others of them want to become psychologists and change individuals.
sentences.zh: 而另一些人则想成为心理学家，改变个人。

sentences.en: And Aristotle told us, by the way, that the two most noble professions were teaching and politics.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，亚里士多德曾告诉我们，最崇高的两个职业是教学和政治。

sentences.en: Well, politics, I think, is about changing the institutions that have gone wrong.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为政治是关于改变那些已经出错的制度。

sentences.en: And I'm all for that.
sentences.zh: 我完全支持这一点。

sentences.en: And psychology is, by and large, about changing the minds, the thinking of individuals.
sentences.zh: 而心理学大体上是关于改变个人的思想和思维。

sentences.en: Now, you can do both.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可以两者兼顾。

sentences.en: Some heads do it better than others.
sentences.zh: 有些领导者比其他人做得更好。

sentences.en: So I'm not a politician.
sentences.zh: 所以我不是政治家。

sentences.en: I'm better at helping individuals find happiness.
sentences.zh: 我更擅长帮助个人寻找幸福。

sentences.en: The art of politics is helping the society find happiness.
sentences.zh: 政治的艺术是帮助社会寻找幸福。

sentences.en: And these two marry pretty well.
sentences.zh: 这两者结合得很好。

sentences.en: They're not in tension.
sentences.zh: 它们并不冲突。

sentences.en: So let me give you an example of something that I work on.
sentences.zh: 让我举一个我正在研究的例子。

sentences.en: So I'm interested in the question of whether or not politically government should measure GDP or happiness in a culture.
sentences.zh: 我对政治政府是否应该衡量GDP还是文化中的幸福感这个问题很感兴趣。

sentences.en: So is the goal of good government more wealth, which is what my economist friends tell me, or is it more happiness?
sentences.zh: 那么，好政府的目标是更多的财富——这是我的经济学家朋友告诉我的——还是更多的幸福？

sentences.en: Happiness.
sentences.zh: 幸福。

sentences.en: Okay?
sentences.zh: 好吗？

sentences.en: So that's an important political issue.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个重要的政治议题。

sentences.en: And politicians argue about this.
sentences.zh: 政治家们对此争论不休。

sentences.en: It's a major issue in England right now, a major issue in New Zealand, a major issue in the Emirates.
sentences.zh: 这目前是英国的一个重大议题，也是新西兰和阿联酋的一个重大议题。

sentences.en: Shouldn't we study both?
sentences.zh: 我们不应该两者都研究吗？

sentences.en: Don't they go hand in hand?
sentences.zh: 它们不是相辅相成的吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so what the politicians do is they ask, which of these things should we matter?
sentences.zh: 所以政治家们所做的是询问，这些事情中哪些应该重要？

sentences.en: What the psychologist says is, well, let's work on good measures of happiness.
sentences.zh: 心理学家所说的是，好吧，让我们致力于建立良好的幸福衡量标准。

sentences.en: And indeed, that complements the political life.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这补充了政治生活。

sentences.en: So to think that there's a tension between the psychology of improving happiness individuals and the psychology of improving a society is often a straw man.
sentences.zh: 因此，认为改善个人幸福的心理学与改善社会的心理学之间存在冲突，往往是一个稻草人谬误。

sentences.en: And by the way,
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，

sentences.en: it's very important within positive psychology that most of the exercises that actually work and produce more individual happiness are exercises like helping another person.
sentences.zh: 在积极心理学中非常重要的一点是，大多数真正有效并能产生更多个人幸福感的练习，都是像帮助他人这样的练习。

sentences.en: So the single most effective antidepressant short exercise we have is, if you're depressed right now, turn this blog off, go out, find someone who needs help, and help them.
sentences.zh: 所以我们拥有的最有效的短期抗抑郁练习是：如果你现在感到抑郁，关掉这个博客，走出去，找到一个需要帮助的人，然后帮助他们。

sentences.en: That's the single best antidepressant we know.
sentences.zh: 这是我们所知的最好的抗抑郁药。

sentences.en: So very often, Chris Peterson's theme, other people matter, as the heart of positive psychology, is indeed at the heart of building individual happiness as well.
sentences.zh: 所以很多时候，克里斯·彼得森（Chris Peterson）的主题——“他人很重要”——作为积极心理学的核心，确实也是建立个人幸福的核心。

sentences.en: So I think there's a straw man here.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这里存在一个稻草人谬误。

sentences.en: I think we can both build individual happiness and we can build the best institutions and correct the institutions that have gone wrong in our society.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们既可以建立个人幸福，也可以建立最好的制度，并纠正我们社会中已经出错的制度。

sentences.en: After all these years of studying positive psychology, what's left?
sentences.zh: 研究了这么多年的积极心理学，还剩下什么？

sentences.en: Are there still some unanswered questions?
sentences.zh: 还有一些未解之谜吗？

sentences.en: Well, there's a huge one, and it's the one I'm working on now.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有一个巨大的问题，也是我目前正在研究的问题。

sentences.en: So I've bitten off a lot more than I can chew,
sentences.zh: 所以我承担的比我能处理的要多得多，

sentences.en: Kim, but let me tell you what I've been writing for the last couple of years, and it will probably go on for a few more years.
sentences.zh: Kim，但让我告诉你我过去几年一直在写的东西，这可能还会持续几年。

sentences.en: The theme of my life's work has been agency, and for me, agency has three components.
sentences.zh: 我毕生工作的主题是“能动性”（Agency），对我来说，能动性有三个组成部分。

sentences.en: The first is what Al Bandura called self-efficacy, efficacy, and that's the belief I can achieve a goal.
sentences.zh: 第一个是阿尔伯特·班杜拉（Al Bandura）所说的自我效能感，即相信我能实现目标。

sentences.en: The second element of agency is optimism and future-mindedness, that I can achieve this goal well into the future.
sentences.zh: 能动性的第二个要素是乐观和未来导向，即相信我能在遥远的未来实现这个目标。

sentences.en: And the third element of agency is imagination, and that's the belief that there are a whole lot of good goals, a whole lot of scenarios that I can achieve well into the future.
sentences.zh: 能动性的第三个要素是想象力，即相信有许多美好的目标，有许多我能在未来实现的场景。

sentences.en: So I've asked the question, what is the world history of agency?
sentences.zh: 所以我提出了一个问题：能动性的世界历史是什么？

sentences.en: And the hypothesis is that when societies and religions and epochs are highly agentic, that they have beliefs in human efficacy, optimism, and imagination,
sentences.zh: 假设是，当社会、宗教和时代具有高度能动性时，即它们相信人类的效能、乐观和想象力时，

sentences.en: that's when progress occurs.
sentences.zh: 进步就会发生。

sentences.en: And by progress, by the way, this is not an arbitrary term, I mean progress in thinking, progress in technology, progress in medicine, progress in the arts, progress in literature,
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这里的“进步”不是一个随意的术语，我指的是思维的进步、技术的进步、医学的进步、艺术的进步、文学的进步，

sentences.en: progress in the quality of human life, and progress in human freedom.
sentences.zh: 人类生活质量的进步，以及人类自由的进步。

sentences.en: So when in history does progress occur?
sentences.zh: 那么历史上什么时候会出现进步？

sentences.en: And the hypothesis is that when the culture believes in agency, that's when progress occurs.
sentences.zh: 假设是，当文化相信能动性时，进步就会发生。

sentences.en: When the culture, when the religion believes in lack of agency, that's when stagnation occurs.
sentences.zh: 当文化、宗教相信缺乏能动性时，停滞就会发生。

sentences.en: And so what I'm doing is going through human history from hunter, fishers, and gatherers up in the West and in China,
sentences.zh: 所以我正在做的是回顾人类历史，从西方的狩猎、捕鱼和采集者到中国，

sentences.en: trying to measure the culture's belief in human agency and progress.
sentences.zh: 试图衡量文化对人类能动性和进步的信仰。

sentences.en: And just for example, I've just published a paper on Greco-Roman thought and agency.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，我刚刚发表了一篇关于希腊罗马思想与能动性的论文。

sentences.en: And basically, if you go back to the Iliad, the Iliad, the gods have it all, and there's no human agency.
sentences.zh: 基本上，如果你回到《伊利亚特》，在《伊利亚特》中，神拥有了一切，没有人类的能动性。

sentences.en: By the Odyssey, humans start to have it.
sentences.zh: 到了《奥德赛》，人类开始拥有它。

sentences.en: And by the golden age of Greek philosophy, it's hugely agentic.
sentences.zh: 到了希腊哲学的黄金时代，它具有极强的能动性。

sentences.en: It's optimistic.
sentences.zh: 它是乐观的。

sentences.en: It's efficacious and imaginative.
sentences.zh: 它是高效且富有想象力的。

sentences.en: And to map into that trend, there's enormous progress in Greco-Roman area.
sentences.zh: 为了映射这一趋势，希腊罗马地区出现了巨大的进步。

sentences.en: And this goes on until about 380 A.D., when Rome is falling apart.
sentences.zh: 这种情况一直持续到公元380年左右，当时罗马正在分崩离析。

sentences.en: And at the time, the early Christian philosophers are enormously agentic.
sentences.zh: 当时，早期的基督教哲学家具有极强的能动性。

sentences.en: And St. Augustine comes along in 384 and says, no, it's all God's agency.
sentences.zh: 圣奥古斯丁在384年出现并说，不，一切都是上帝的能动性。

sentences.en: If you happen to do something good, happen to avoid evil, it's entirely God's grace.
sentences.zh: 如果你碰巧做了一件好事，碰巧避免了邪恶，那完全是上帝的恩典。

sentences.en: And it is my view that Augustine's view of Christianity, which becomes Catholic doctrine for almost 1,000 years, produces the stagnation of the Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 我的观点是，奥古斯丁的基督教观——它在近1000年里成为了天主教教义——导致了中世纪的停滞。

sentences.en: So, and indeed, my colleagues in China have just done the same analysis for Chinese culture through the Greco-Roman period.
sentences.zh: 所以，事实上，我在中国的同事刚刚对中国文化在希腊罗马时期的表现做了同样的分析。

sentences.en: And again, the same kind of things occur.
sentences.zh: 同样，也发生了类似的事情。

sentences.en: So, what I'm working on right now, and for me, the big question in positive psychology,
sentences.zh: 所以，我目前正在研究的，对我来说是积极心理学中的大问题，

sentences.en: is this just a peculiar Western idea of the 21st century in which it's a good idea to be positive?
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是21世纪一种独特的西方观念，即保持积极是一种好主意吗？

sentences.en: Or is there a human history of this?
sentences.zh: 还是说这背后有人类历史的支撑？

sentences.en: And I think there is a human history.
sentences.zh: 我认为确实有人类历史。

sentences.en: It translates into agency.
sentences.zh: 它转化为能动性。

sentences.en: And I think it's the controlling engine of human progress.
sentences.zh: 我认为它是人类进步的控制引擎。

sentences.en: And just to say one more thing, Kim, about what I'm working on here.
sentences.zh: Kim，关于我正在研究的内容，再多说一句。

sentences.en: Many different fields have tried to do the history of the world.
sentences.zh: 许多不同的领域都试图书写世界历史。

sentences.en: And so, the greatest one recently is Jared Diamond, in which Diamond basically argues that ecology is at the center of human progress.
sentences.zh: 最近最伟大的著作当属贾雷德·戴蒙德的作品，戴蒙德在书中主要论证了生态学是人类进步的核心。

sentences.en: And what I'm trying to do right now is to say, no, the center of human progress is a mental process called agency.
sentences.zh: 而我现在想说的是，不，人类进步的核心是一种被称为“能动性”的心理过程。

sentences.en: It's that agency that has produced human progress.
sentences.zh: 正是这种能动性推动了人类的进步。

sentences.en: So, I want to do for psychology what Jared Diamond did for ecology.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想在心理学领域做贾雷德·戴蒙德在生态学领域所做的事情。

sentences.en: But one of the important differences, if you believe just Diamond's theory, it doesn't leave you with any interventions for children and for the future.
sentences.zh: 但一个重要的区别在于，如果你只相信戴蒙德的理论，它无法为你提供任何针对儿童或未来的干预手段。

sentences.en: So, we can't change the climate very much.
sentences.zh: 我们无法大幅改变气候。

sentences.en: We can't change the direction in which the rivers flow.
sentences.zh: 我们无法改变河流的流向。

sentences.en: But we can change the belief in agency.
sentences.zh: 但我们可以改变对能动性的信念。

sentences.en: That sounds like an absolutely astonishing project.
sentences.zh: 这听起来是一个极其宏大的计划。

sentences.en: And I look forward to seeing you complete that.
sentences.zh: 我很期待看到你完成它。

sentences.en: It sounds like a lifetime of work.
sentences.zh: 这听起来需要毕生的精力去投入。

sentences.en: My hat is off to you, Dr. Seligman.
sentences.zh: 塞利格曼博士，我向您致敬。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us today, Dr. Seligman.
sentences.zh: 感谢您今天来到我们的节目，塞利格曼博士。

sentences.en: You've given our listeners a great deal of good information to think about and to work on things that they can take into their lives and act upon.
sentences.zh: 您为我们的听众提供了大量有价值的信息，让他们可以思考并付诸实践，应用到自己的生活中。

sentences.en: Oh, thanks for having me, Kim.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢你邀请我，金。

sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 或任何您获取播客的平台上收听《心理学谈话》往期节目。

sentences.zh: 如果您对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，请发送电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.zh: 我们的音频编辑是克里斯·康达扬。

sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。
